p: Reading is one of those towns that gets overlooked, but it has more going for it than many people realise. It's a major business hub, a university town and the home of one of the country's best-known music festivals every August bank holiday. It's also got a long history, with the ruins of an abbey founded by Henry I right in the centre.

Reading station is one of the busiest outside London, with fast trains to Paddington and the Elizabeth line also reaching the town. It's also a big hub for trains heading west and north. If you're driving, the M4 runs to the south of the town, and there are plenty of car parks around the centre.

For a group outing, booking ahead helps, especially at weekends. Agree on a rough timetable, sort out teams and make sure everyone knows where to meet. Games bars are a great way to bring together a mixed crowd, as there's something for everyone, whether they're natural competitors or just along for the laughs.

If you've got a day to spare, the Museum of English Rural Life in town is a quirky free museum full of farming history and countryside stories. Reading Museum, in the town hall, has a full-size Victorian replica of the Bayeux Tapestry, which is worth a look. And the Thames Path heads out from town towards Sonning and Pangbourne if you fancy a riverside walk before your evening of games.
